content: Engaging in physical exercise while experiencing microvascular complications, such as peripheral neuropathy, requires careful consideration. Peripheral neuropathy is characterized by a diminished ability to perceive pain and an elevated pain threshold in the extremities. This condition can lead to an increased risk of skin breakdown, infections, and the development of Charcot joint destruction during certain types of physical activity. Consequently, it is essential to conduct a comprehensive evaluation to confirm that neuropathy does not impair kinesthetic or proprioceptive sensations during exercise, especially in individuals with more advanced stages of neuropathy.
